speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your symptoms of fever, night sweats, weight loss, and abdominal pain, please tell me if you have noticed any recent changes in your bowel habits or stool color. Also, do you have any history of liver disease or jaundice? REQUEST TEST: Liver function tests, bilirubin, and Amylase.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your normal liver and pancreatic enzyme results, I need to determine the source of the lymphadenopathy and abdominal pain. Has the pain in your abdomen been specifically in the right upper quadrant or upper left side, and have you noticed any lumps or swelling there? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CTA_and_Chest_CT.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Burkitt Lymphoma. The constellation of "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss), abdominal pain, early satiety, supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and the rapid onset over four weeks is highly suspicious for an aggressive B-cell lymphoma, particularly given the abdominal involvement. The normal liver and pancreatic enzymes help rule out acute hepatitis or pancreatitis, while the CT scans likely reveal characteristic "starry sky" infiltration or massive lymphadenopathy requiring biopsy confirmation.
